title: Rent Agreements, Deposits and Eviction
summary: What a good rent agreement contains, how deposits work, and the rules on notice and eviction.
sectionRefs: Tamil Nadu Regulation of Rights and Responsibilities of Landlords and Tenants Act, 2017

body.text: A rent agreement is a contract, and both the tenant and the landlord have rights. A clear written agreement prevents most disputes.
What a good rent agreement should contain

items: Rent amount, due date and mode of payment.
Security deposit amount and when it is returned.
Notice period for leaving, or for asking a tenant to leave.
Who pays maintenance, electricity and water.
Right to live peacefully without unlawful eviction.
Right to get the security deposit back as agreed.
Right to essential services such as water and electricity.
Right to proper notice before being asked to leave.
Right to receive rent on time.
Right to get the property back at the end of the term.
Right to a fair deposit for possible damage.
A landlord must give proper written notice before asking a tenant to leave; the period is set by the agreement or the rent law.
Eviction usually needs a valid ground, such as non-payment of rent or the landlord's genuine need.
A tenant must also give notice before leaving, as agreed.
A landlord cannot lock a tenant out, cut off water or electricity, or remove belongings to force an exit. That is unlawful and can be challenged in court.
The security deposit should be returned as agreed, minus genuine unpaid dues or damage beyond normal wear.
Repairs are usually split: structural repairs by the landlord, small day-to-day repairs by the tenant.

body.text: The Model Tenancy Act, 2021 sets a common framework: a written agreement, a cap on security deposits (generally two months' rent for residential premises) and a Rent Authority for disputes.
No one may take the law into their own hands. Locking a tenant out or cutting utilities to force an exit is unlawful.
Always keep a signed copy of the agreement and receipts for rent and deposit.

practicalSteps: Put everything in a written, signed agreement.
Pay rent by bank transfer so there is a record.
Keep receipts for the deposit and for any major repairs.
For disputes, approach the Rent Authority or a civil court rather than taking the law into your own hands.
exceptions: Rent laws differ from state to state, and older tenancies may follow older Rent Control Acts.
The Model Tenancy Act applies only where a state has adopted it.

faqs.q: Can my landlord increase the rent anytime?
faqs.a: Only as allowed by your agreement or the applicable rent law, usually with proper notice.

faqs.q: Can the landlord keep my deposit for normal wear and tear?
faqs.a: No. A deposit can be adjusted only for unpaid dues or actual damage beyond normal use, as set out in the agreement.

sources.label: Model Tenancy Act, 2021 - Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

misconceptions.myth: The landlord can evict me any time.
misconceptions.fact: Eviction must follow the agreement and the law, usually with written notice and, if disputed, an order from a court or Rent Authority.
